results.title: DigitalOcean GPU Droplets: cards, regions, billing - AI Hosting Index
results.author: George D
highlights:
Last updated 6 November 2026 · . By George

DigitalOcean rents whole GPU servers, called GPU Droplets, with NVIDIA H100, H200, L40S, RTX 4000 Ada and RTX 6000 Ada cards and AMD MI300X cards. It bills by the second, with 60 seconds at least, and the bill runs until you destroy the Droplet.

Each price covers the whole machine: the GPU, processor cores, memory and disks. This guide lists the plans and regions from DigitalOcean's own documentation, read on 6 November 2026, with prices from our weekly price records.

- 2 hours the least notice DigitalOcean gives before it takes back a spot GPU Droplet Official page, 6 Nov 2026

...

...

## Prices of the GPU Droplets in our records

DigitalOcean GPU Droplets. Prices checked on 1 Nov 2026.

| Plan | Price | New-customer offer | Link |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DigitalOcean GPU Droplet, 1 x NVIDIA L40S 48 GB GPU | $1.57/hour (about $1,146/month) on demand, billed per second · VAT not stated checked 1 Nov 2026 | New accounts get a $5 credit that lasts 90 days and covers every product except SaaS add-ons checked 1 Nov 2026 | Visit |
| DigitalOcean GPU Droplet, 1 x NVIDIA H100 80 GB GPU | $4.41/hour (about $3,219/month) on demand, billed per second · VAT not stated checked 1 Nov 2026 | New accounts get a $5 credit that lasts 90 days and covers every product except SaaS add-ons checked 1 Nov 2026 | Visit |
| DigitalOcean GPU Droplet, 8 x NVIDIA H100 8× 80 GB GPUs | $35.28/hour (about $25,754/month) on demand, billed per second; price for the whole 8-GPU machine · VAT not stated checked 1 Nov 2026 | New accounts get a $5 credit that lasts 90 days and covers every product except SaaS add-ons checked 1 Nov 2026 | Visit |

Monthly costs for hourly prices assume the server runs all month (730 hours), or less where a provider caps the monthly bill.

Whole servers, by the hour, billed by the second. The L40S Droplet has 8 vCPUs and 64 GiB of memory.

Hourly price of one L40S or one H100, in US dollars Current price checks of DigitalOcean's and Runpod's pages. Prices checked on 1 Nov 2026.

 $0 $2 $4 $6 DigitalOcean GPU Droplet, 1 x NVIDIA L40S $1.57/hour (about $1,146/month) Runpod L40S $1.09/hour (about $796/month) DigitalOcean GPU Droplet, 1 x NVIDIA H100 $4.41/hour (about $3,219/month) Runpod H100 PCIe $2.89/hour (about $2,110/month)

...

## How the bill works

- By the second: billing starts when you create the Droplet and stops when you destroy it, with 60 seconds at least.
- Powered off is still billed: the GPU stays reserved for you, so switching the Droplet off does not stop the charge.
- No monthly ceiling: the 672-hour monthly cap of DigitalOcean's ordinary Droplets does not apply to GPU Droplets.
- Spot machines: in public preview, at a daily price never above on-demand. DigitalOcean gives at least 2 hours' notice before it takes one back.
- Data transfer: incoming traffic and traffic inside your private network are free. Outgoing traffic above your team's pooled allowance is billed by the gigabyte.

New accounts may be charged partway through the month when they create GPU Droplets. DigitalOcean says the total does not change.

...

## How we checked

We read DigitalOcean's Droplet features page, its GPU availability page and its Droplet pricing documentation on 6 November 2026. DigitalOcean last verified the availability page on 10 August 2026.

This analysis lists the published on-demand list prices per GPU-hour for H100, H200 and L40S at the tracked providers, each with its source and access date, and normalises them per GB of GPU memory and per TB/s of memory bandwidth. Prices stay in each provider's own currency and billing basis. Several providers offer a GPU without publishing an hourly price; they appear as available but unpriced.

...

1. 01 Prices are published in different currencies (USD and TRY), so no cross-provider ranking is computed on this page.
2. 02 Billing granularity differs: per second with a minimum charge, per minute, or hourly. Short jobs can cost more than the hourly price implies on coarse billing.
3. 03 Some GPUs are offered without public prices (for example PortvMind H200/L40S and several hyperscaler configurations); they are marked as unpriced rather than estimated.
4. 04 Per-GPU-hour list prices exclude storage, data transfer and host resources that some providers bundle and others bill separately.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.

highlights:
H100 rate cards ran from $1.99 to $9.80 a GPU-hour on 8 October 2026. Large buyers rarely pay them. How GPU deals close, and how to benchmark a quote.

Each rate is the provider's own published figure, read from its pricing page on 8 October 2026. A rate marked "from" is the lowest tier on the page. Casitel OS reads these rate cards every day: on 3 November 2026 the median H100 list price across nine GPU clouds was $3.90 an hour.

...

A list price is for one GPU, today, with no commitment. A large deal changes every one of those terms.

- Term. A commitment of one year or more is priced below on-demand. DigitalOcean, for example, publishes $3.26 a GPU-hour for an H100 on a 12-month reservation.
- Volume. A cluster of thousands of GPUs is a different product from a single instance. The seller fills a whole hall at once.
- Payment. A deposit or prepayment buys a lower rate. It also moves risk from the seller to the buyer.
- Start date and place. Capacity that is live today costs more than capacity that goes live next year. A region with spare power costs less than one without.
- What is in the hour. Fast networking between GPUs, storage, support and data transfer are priced in some quotes and added on in others.

results.title: RunPod Secure Cloud GPU Rates Rise: H100 $3.99, B200 $7.99
results.author: TSN Newsroom
highlights:
A GPU price tracker, GPU Economy, says RunPod raised 12 of its 29 on-demand Secure Cloud GPU rates on 8 October 2026 [1]. RunPod’s pricing page now shows the higher prices [2]. RunPod made no announcement that we could find, so the timing and the old prices rest on the tracker.

## The new rates

RunPod sells two tiers, Secure Cloud and Community Cloud; on its listings the Community rates are lower. Prices are in US dollars per GPU per hour, on demand, meaning pay as you go. GPU Economy reports [1]:

| GPU | Before | Now | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $3.49 | $3.99 | +14.3% |
| H200 | $4.59 | $5.29 | +15.3% |
| B200 | $6.79 | $7.99 | +17.7% |
| B300 | $7.89 | $8.99 | +13.9% |

The H100, H200, B200 and B300 are Nvidia data-centre chips used to train and run AI models. The tracker says the 12 rises came “between our reads of October 8, 2026 at 15:41 and 16:41 UTC”, which is 16:41 and 17:41 in London. It also computes that one H100 SXM running for a 730-hour month went from $2,547.70 to $2,912.70.

...

The tracker says “None of the 35 Community Cloud on-demand rates changed in the same read”: the H100 SXM there stayed at $2.69 and the B200 at $5.98 [1].

## What RunPod’s page shows

RunPod’s pricing page lists $3.99/hr for the H100 SXM, $7.99/hr for the B200, $5.29/hr for the H200 and $8.99/hr for the B300 [2]. But the page is labelled “Updated September 27, 2026”, which does not match the tracker’s 8 October timing. The page’s hidden structured data, the code search engines read, still lists the old Secure Cloud prices, such as $3.49 for the H100 SXM [2]. The tracker says it read RunPod’s public API, and that on 9 October the page’s own markup still carried $3.49 [1]. That fits what we see.

results.author: Jose Mir
highlights:
What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

By the numbers:

- Nebius list price for an H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour; B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- The Ornn H100 index settled at $3.17 on October 23, up about 4% in a month.
